reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended Repeatedly re-rendering historical tool results adds unnecessary serialization and dataframe-conversion overhead that grows with accumulated tool output, even when citations are unused.
1 open issue - [Avoid rerendering historical tool results on every streamed response](https://github.com/posit-dev/chatlas/pull/487#discussion_r4515733765) · New
What changed in this PR Fixes #381 by including documents embedded in tool results when resolving Anthropic `document_index` citations, keeping later citations aligned with their sources. **Changes:** - Counts raw tool-result documents, resolving URL sources and preserving empty slots for non-URL sources. - Excludes search results, which use separate citation indices. - Adds a regression test and changelog entry. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | tests/​test_provider_anthropic.py | Tests citation alignment across tool-result documents, search results, and a later web fetch. | | chatlas/​_provider_anthropic.py | Includes raw tool-result documents in citation source indexing. | | CHANGELOG.md | Documents the citation-resolution fix. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: This re-renders every historical tool result for each response and each streamed text-block stop, even without citations. Ordinary JSON and dataframe results contribute no document slots but incur repeated serialization and potentially `to_pandas()` conversions, adding work proportional to the accumulated tool output. Reuse rendered model values or bypass results known to be text-only, while preserving custom `to_json()` methods that can return raw blocks.

Addressed in 9bfa2e5: `anthropic_tool_result_document_sources()` now returns early unless `model_format="as_is"` — the only format whose model value can be a list of raw blocks; every other format serializes to a string, so rendering it just to find no blocks was wasted work. This means a custom `to_json()` that returns raw blocks rather than a JSON string would no longer be counted, but that violates the documented contract of `to_json()` and wasn't worth reintroducing per-citation serialization.
